data.note:
Unblinding check: specimen s_7526ba207c is AZ-C, BBBC021 annotation Eg5 inhibitors. My blinded conclusion was Eg5 inhibitors p=0.68 – correct by code.

Evidence led: 4/4 wells NSC Eg5 with similarities 0.75-0.83 (e9), top neighbor AZ138 Eg5 reference (mean sim 0.816 vs 0.746 for vincristine destabilizer). Phenotype consistent with Eg5 inhibition: dose-dependent tubulin mean/std increase (z +15 to +28, rho=+1.0, e10) with bright heterogeneous tubulin bundles and mitotic-like rounded cells with condensed DNA on composite (e4), reduced nuclear solidity (z -9.5 to -28, e2/e3/e7/e8), increased DNA integrated (z +12-16) and frac_large_nucleus (z ~10-13). Microscopist flagged microtubule-targeting mitotic arrest, top candidate Microtubule stabilizers but noting inability to separate stabilizer/destabilizer/Eg5 without spindle resolution.

Post-unblinding note: PubChem has no structure for internal code AZ-C (as flagged), ChEMBL no curated mechanism – relying on BBBC021 annotation. Literature supports interpretation: Eg5 inhibitors induce monopolar spindle formation and mitotic arrest; e.g. K858, a novel Eg5 inhibitor, induces mitotic arrest and cell death PMID 19351824; pyrenocine A induces monopolar spindle formation via Eg5-related mechanisms PMID 31679979; HDAC inhibitor-induced mitotic arrest is mediated by Eg5/KIF11 acetylation PMID 28392145, illustrating the Eg5-dependent spindle phenotype.

Next step proposed remains high-resolution tubulin/gamma-tubulin monopolar spindle quantification + pH3 to confirm Eg5 mechanism vs microtubule destabilizer control.

reflection.text:
Post-unblinding reflection — AZ-C verified as Eg5 inhibitors, called correctly at p=0.68. This is a research phenotype screen, not a clinical finding.

### What the evidence got right

The core call rested on 4 wells spanning 0.01-1 uM, all rep 1, that were remarkably consistent:
- e2 (1 uM): tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2, tub_mean z=+28.5, nuc_solidity z=-28.3, n=295 cells
- e3 (0.1 uM): nuc_solidity z=-21.0, tub_std z=+19.7, tub_mean z=+17.2
- e7 (0.3 uM): tub_std z=+19.0, tub_mean z=+17.9, nuc_solidity z=-15.6
- e8 (0.01 uM): tub_mean z=+15.3, nuc_dna_integrated z=+14.8, tub_std z=+14.6

That is a massive tubulin intensity/texture increase with decreased solidity at every dose tested. e10 dose_response made this explicit: tub_mean Spearman rho =+1.00 (p=0) over the 4 doses. This monotonic, high-magnitude tubulin phenotype is characteristic of mitotic arrest involving spindle perturbation, consistent with Eg5/KIF11 inhibition described in literature returned in this run e16 — e.g. Eg5 inhibition and monopolar spindle/mitotic arrest themes in PMID 19351824, PMID 31679979, PMID 28392145, without needing to claim the screen measured spindle polarity directly.

Comparison to atlas was decisive when interpreted correctly: e5 NSC 2/2 Eg5 and e9 NSC 4/4 Eg5 after the full 4-well set. That per-well NSC unanimity drove the hypothesis update e6 0.45 -> e13 0.68. The negative controls via dose_response also worked: e11 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.20 (p=0.8) and e12 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 (p=0.6) showed no increase in large/polyploid nuclei with dose, which argues against Aurora kinase inhibitors that typically drive large nuclei/polyploidy, correctly dropping Aurora 0.07 -> 0.04.

### What was ambiguous / could have misled and why

1. **Atlas k-neighbour split:** e5 and e9 both reported k-neighbour 5/10 Eg5 inhibitors, 5/10 Microtubule destabilizers. On pooled neighbours this looks like a tie. The agent was right not to treat it as a tie — NSC vote was 4/4 Eg5 — but this explains why the review correctly called p=0.68 calibrated rather than >0.9. The dataset alone with pooled neighbours cannot fully resolve Eg5 vs destabilizer by profile similarity alone.

2. **Microscopist phenotype e4:** “density lower vs DMSO; candidates: Microtubule stabilizers, Microtubule destabilizers, Aurora kinase inhibitors” — this was intentionally non-specific. Tubulin increase alone (e2/e3) initially supported stabilizers at 0.20 in e6, because stabilizers also increase tubulin intensity. The agent correctly down-weighted stabilizers to 0.12 in e13 after repeat atlas e9 showed zero stabilizer neighbours, even though e10 rho=+1.00 could superficially fit a stabilizer. e15 lookup confirming AZ-C has no curated mechanism/name in PubChem/ChEMBL meant we had to rely on phenotype, not annotation, which increased that initial ambiguity.

3. **No direct spindle polarity readout:** We never acquired monopolar vs bipolar spindle quantification. e4 noted lower density but no spindle count, and our features were only tub_mean/tub_std/tub_glcm_contrast + nuc_solidity/DNA. That is sensitive for mitotic arrest but cannot by itself distinguish Eg5 monopolar spindles from destabilizer-compromised spindles. The proposed next experiment — alpha-tubulin + gamma-tubulin/pericentrin high-resolution IF for monopolar fraction plus phospho-histone H3 — is exactly what would resolve this.

### Acquisition choices — strengths and misses

**Strengths:** Sampling high (1 uM) then mid (0.1 uM) then filling 0.3 and 0.01 uM gave a 100-fold dose spread. This was discriminative enough that the review noted a replicate or lower dose would have been unlikely to overturn the call with budget exhausted (e1: 4 of 4 wells left for this compound). It established that the effect was already near-maximal at 0.01 uM (z=+15.3) and monotonically increasing, not transient toxicity at top dose.

**Misses/limitations:**
- All 4 wells were rep 1; no rep 2 was acquired at any dose, so inter-well biological variance could not be estimated. The conclusion rests on consistency across doses rather than true replication.
- Lowest available doses 0.0003-0.003 uM were not sampled, so threshold/EC50 was not defined — e8 was already strongly positive.
- We did not acquire dedicated polyploidy/mitotic markers; we inferred from frac_large_nucleus and nuc_dna_integrated dose_response (e11/e12) which are indirect.
- Literature search e17 for “microtubule destabilizer vs stabilizer mitotic phenotype MCF-7” returned 0 hits, so we had no run-internal literature to sharpen destabilizer vs Eg5 distinction beyond atlas.

Overall, e2/e3/e7/e8 + e10 provided the strong, dose-dependent tubulin/solidity signal, e5/e9 NSC provided class anchoring, and e11/e12 excluded Aurora, supporting Eg5 0.68 with ~0.27 retained for other microtubule mechanisms — a calibrated outcome validated on unblinding.

- e5/e9 k-neighbour 5/10 Eg5 5/10 destabilizer tie could have been over-interpreted as equal probability; required NSC unanimity to favour Eg5
- e4 and tub increase alone initially plausibly fit microtubule stabilizers (0.20 in e6) — phenotype features are non-specific for subclass without spindle polarity imaging
- No rep 2 and no doses below 0.01 uM acquired, so reproducibility and threshold not defined; conclusion relied on cross-dose consistency

Proposed next experiment: As proposed: high-resolution alpha-tubulin + pericentrin/gamma-tubulin IF to quantify monopolar vs bipolar spindles and PH3 FACS for mitotic index vs Eg5 inhibitor and microtubule destabilizer controls.
